title: Repeated holdout validation for weighted quantile sum regression.
ehr_evidence: Our example data comes from a study of prenatal exposure to 26 endocrine disrupting chemicals in relation to child Intelligence Quotient (IQ) among mother-child pairs from the Swedish Environmental Longitudinal, Mother and Child, Asthma and Allergy (SELMA) study, a birth cohort study; exposures were measured from biospecimens and IQ from clinical testing, not from electronic health records or administrative data.
summary: Methods paper proposing repeated holdout validation for weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression, demonstrated on 718 mother-child pairs from the SELMA birth cohort assessing prenatal exposure to 26 endocrine disrupting chemicals and child IQ.
key_findings: Single-partition WQS index estimate was significant on the full dataset (β = -2.20, 95% CI -3.43 to -0.98) but attenuated and nonsignificant with repeated holdout validation (β = -0.83, 95% CI -2.11 to 0.45).
Repeated holdout results were attenuated toward the null and nonsignificant compared to training and testing on the full dataset (resubstitution error).
Repeated holdout median estimation gave β = -0.86 (95% CI -1.99 to 0.43).
DPHP had the second-highest mean weight (10%) but 7 of 100 repeated holdouts fell below the 3.8% chemical-of-concern threshold, illustrating instability of single partitions.
Triclosan mean weight (3%) was below the threshold, yet 26% of repetitions exceeded it.
captured_features: Concentrations of 26 endocrine disrupting chemicals (triclosan, bisphenols A/F/S, phthalate metabolites, PFAS, HCB, Nonachlor, DDT/DDT metabolite, summed PCBs)
Chemical weights and WQS index β coefficients
pathologies_diseases: None (outcome is child IQ, a neurodevelopmental measure, not a disease)
study_design: Cohort (method-validation study applied to SELMA birth cohort data)
population: 718 mother-child pairs from the SELMA study in Sweden; prenatal chemical exposure assessed in relation to child IQ
exposure_domain: Endocrine disrupting chemical mixtures (triclosan, bisphenols, phthalates, PFAS, organochlorines, PCBs)
limitations: Computationally intensive, taking ~100x longer than typical WQS implementations.
Training-test split percentages are somewhat arbitrary (40%/60% used).
A larger number of repetitions would provide better normal approximations.
Single partitions may lead to incorrect conclusions about individual chemicals of concern.
data_availability_statement: E.M. Tanner, C. Gennings, evamtanner/Repeated_Holdout_WQS: 1st Rodeo (Version v1.0.0). [WWW Document]. Zenodo., (2019), doi:http://dx.doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.2658697.
